To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hallmarks of human cancer can be targeted with a rational approach to cancer therapy, and that this approach has the potential to improve the efficacy and safety of cancer treatment.

(1) cancer is a disease of the genome; (2) the genetic changes in the genome of cancer cells can be grouped into six categories; and (3) the genetic changes that occur in cancer are similar to those that occur during normal development.

1) the molecular and cellular processes that sustain cancer progression are the same for all cancers, 2) these processes are not unique to cancer cells but are also present in normal stem and progenitor (NSP) cells and in their microenvironment (i.e. the stroma, the immune system, and the vasculature) and 3) the same molecular mechanisms are involved in both NSP cell and cancer cell functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular basis for the development and progression of human cancer and the application of our findings to the development of improved diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic strategies for cancer.
identifying and characterizing the molecular basis of the Hallmarks of cancer.
the identification and characterization of the molecular and cellular processes involved in cancer progression and metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 'Hallmarks' concept has been a powerful tool in the development of new cancer treatments.
targeting cancer cells with a single agent, or a few agents, will be insufficient.
the Hallmarks of cancer are a useful guide for the rational development of next generation cancer therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer is a disease of the genome.
cancer is a disease of developmental plasticity, which requires a systemic approach.
cancer is an extremely complex disease that requires the acquisition of a number of biological capabilities to develop.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hallmarks of the disease are not only the targets of therapy, but also the drivers of resistance to therapy.

the concept of Hallmarks of cancer provides an effective framework for understanding the molecular nature of cancer and for developing new strategies of early detection, treatment and quality-of-life improvement for patients.
we can now identify the molecular mechanisms of the hallmarks of cancers.
